    All Classes and Interfaces

    Classes
    Class
    Description
    Cat
    cat: prints the contents of one or more files to standard out, in order.
    Grep
    grep <pattern> [<file>...]: prints every line, from the given files or from standard input, that matches the regular expression pattern.
    Head
    head [-n <count>] [<file>...]: prints the first count lines (default 10) of each file.
    Ls
    ls [<path>...]: lists files and directories.
    Pwd
    pwd: prints the current working directory.
    Shell
    A simple shell that mimics some basic features of bash.
    ShellCommand
    Abstract class for shared logic of shell commands.
    Sleep
    sleep <seconds>: blocks for the given (fractional) number of seconds, then exits.
    Sort
    sort [-r] [<file>...]: reads every line from all given files (or standard input, if none given), concatenated in argument order, and prints them sorted lexicographically — ascending by default, descending with -r.
    Tail
    tail [-n <count>] [<file>...]: prints the last count lines (default 10) of each file.
    Uniq
    uniq [-c] [<file>]: collapses runs of adjacent duplicate lines into a single line — non-adjacent duplicates are left alone, same as real uniq (pair with sort first to dedupe an entire file).
    Wc
    wc [<file>...]: prints newline, word, and byte counts for each file, and a total line if more than one file is specified.
